Her ne kadar bu, Federal Reserve'ün parasal genişleme anlamına gelmese ve ABD hükümetinin borcunu azaltmayacak olsa da, politika, piyasanın mali baskılara ve uzun vadeli borçlanma maliyetlerine odaklanmasını güçlendirdiğinin sinyalini veriyor. Sonuç olarak altın "çift yönlü fayda" elde etti. 21 Ağustos Doğu Saati'nde spot altın (XAUUSD), ABD Hazinesi'nin uzun vadeli tahvil geri alımlarını genişletmesinin etkisiyle 4.600 doları kırdı. Bu politika ikili bir artış yaratıyor: Düşen getiriler altının elde tutma maliyetlerini azaltıyor ve doları zayıflatıyor; mali açıklardan kaynaklanan artan getiriler ise devlet kredisini ve güvenli liman talebini artırıyor. Teknik olarak altın, önemli hareketli ortalamaları aşarak 0,618 Fibonacci seviyesini aşarak 4.528,85 doları gördü ve 4.700 doları hedefledi. Ancak potansiyel enerji kaynaklı enflasyon ve faiz artırımı beklentileri dönemsel kısıtlamalar yaratıyor. buyback_news.article_context_original: Spot gold (XAUUSD) breached the $4,600 mark on August 21, Eastern Time, and is advancing toward $4,700, marking the first time gold has returned to this price level since May 15. The immediate catalyst driving the rally was the U.S. Department of the Treasury's unexpected expansion of its long-term Treasury buyback program. Although this does not constitute Federal Reserve quantitative easing nor will it reduce U.S. government debt, the policy signal reinforced market focus on fiscal pressures and long-end borrowing costs. As a result, gold has reaped a "dual-path benefit." On August 21 Eastern Time, spot gold (XAUUSD) broke $4,600, driven by the US Treasury’s expansion of long-term bond buybacks. This policy creates a dual-pathway boost: falling yields reduce gold's holding costs and weaken the dollar, while rising yields driven by fiscal deficits heighten sovereign credit and safe-haven demand. Technically, gold has surpassed key moving averages and the 0.618 Fibonacci level at $4,528.85, targeting $4,700. However, potential energy-driven inflation and rate-hike expectations pose periodic constraints. Sustaining support above the 5-day moving average is critical to maintaining the bullish structure toward $4,891.54. Although it is not quantitative easing by the Federal Reserve and will not reduce US government debt, its policy signal reinforced market focus on fiscal pressure and long-end financing costs. Gold thus benefits from a "dual-pathway" boost. By buying back 10- to 30-year Treasuries, the Treasury Department improves long-term bond liquidity and eases the upward pressure on yields. If long-term Treasury yields, especially real yields, pull back, the opportunity cost of holding gold—a non-yielding asset—will decline.
